fix: An achene is a dry one-seeded fruit. It is not a seed, so 'achene(s)' should map to PO_0030107, or to fruit (PO_0009001), and never to seed.
reason: The quality 'broadly oval' (elliptic) is right, but it is said of the achene, which is a fruit. In Carex the achene sits inside the perigynium.
'Perennials' as the first word of the description means the whole plant has a perennial life span.

fix: When 'awnless' sits inside a phrase like 'X of a single awnless scale', the absence belongs to that sub-part (here the pedicellate spikelet). It should not be stated for the taxon's awn in general.
reason: The same text says the sessile spikelet has 'the awn perfect, 2-3 cm long'. Without the pedicellate-spikelet context, 'awn absent' contradicts the source.
The filament is pubescent at its base, and the base part restriction is captured. 'White' describes the hairs and can be left out without making the statement false.
'Ovaire ... 1-loculaire' means the ovary has one locule.
The berry is ca. 6 mm in diameter, and berry maps to fruit. The 'ca.' could be recorded as approximate, but the value is right.
The calyx segments (sepals) have acute apices. Putting the apex shape on the sepal follows the usual convention.
'Corolla ... white or greenish-white' gives two alternative colours of the corolla, and both are mapped correctly.
'Stem leaves ... densely arranged' means the leaves are crowded.
'Sepals unequal, ovate to lanceolate' is a shape range on the sepals, and both values are correct.
The standard petal is pubescent on the outside, so using the petal abaxial epidermis is acceptable. 'Appressed' can be left out without making the statement false.
Each bract subtends 2 flowers, so a flower count of 2 per bract is right. The bract container should be read as 'per bract'.
The lower glume ranges from glabrous to villous. The bearer and the range of hairiness are right.

fix: When secondary veins are counted 'on each side of midvein', they are counted per leaf blade. The container should not be vascular bundle (PO_0005020), which the pipeline likely chose because of its synonym 'vein'.
reason: The count (4-8, up to 12) and the each-side position relative to the midvein are right. But the container says '4-8 secondary veins per vascular bundle', which is not what the flora says.

target: a non-comparative 'rounded' apex shape value (not FLOPO_0980236 'more rounded')
fix: Plain 'rounded' was mapped to the comparative class 'more rounded'. A positive 'rounded' should map to a non-comparative rounded value. The 'apex' should also go to the apex position or part slot.
reason: The flora says the apex is rounded, obtuse or subacute, which is an absolute shape and not a comparison. Obtuse and subacute are right.
'Involucral bracts ... usually not sheathed' is correctly a negated sheathing on the bract, with the frequency 'usually'.

target: place: on veins (abaxial side), i.e. the scales on the abaxial veins
fix: 'Colour on veins' must keep the place slot (leaf vein, on the abaxial side). Without it, a colour seen only on the veins is stated for the whole blade.
reason: The blade is silvery scaly underneath. Only the veins are brownish when young, so 'leaf lamina brown when young' is false as stated.
The stipules are adnate to the petiole. 'Only at base' narrows this but does not make it false.
'Inflorescence ... several-flowered' means flowers are present, several per inflorescence.
Resinous dots on a Vernonia leaf are glandular dots, so gland-dotted is acceptable. 'Both sides' can be left out without making the statement false.
Leaves are broadly elliptic to ovate. The range and the 'broadly' qualifier are captured.
'Subcylindric-campanulate' is mainly campanulate, so campanulate marked approximate is a fair reading.
The calyx is inflated in fruit, and the fruit-development stage context is present.
'Tiges juxtaposées' means the stems stand side by side, close together, which matches approximate (close but not fused).
The petiole (like the rachis) is very sparsely hairy, so pubescent on the petiole is right.
'Shrub or small tree' gives two alternative habits of the whole plant.

target: petal claw (no PO term; petal with a 'claw' part slot), compared to the petal lamina
fix: In 'petal claw about as long as blade', both sides of the comparison are parts of the petal. The bearer is the claw, not the whole petal.
reason: The length ratio of 1 relates the claw to the blade. As written, the annotation says the whole petal is as long as the blade, which is false.
The peduncles are unbranched.

fix: With 'pauci- à multiflores' (few- to many-flowered), the prefix range was cut to its first word. Both ends ('few', 'many') must be kept as a range.
reason: Flowers being present is right, but the count word records only 'few'. The flora says the racemes have few to many flowers.
The racemes are 2-4 cm long. Inflorescence length is right.
